descriptionChirho: A split or disagreement within a group of people, producing factions or opposing parties; used of divisions among crowds about Jesus (John 7:43, 9:16, 10:19), among church members at Corinth (1 Cor 1:10, 11:18, 12:25). Spanish 'división/divisiones' (division/divisions) captures the factional sense; Hindi 'फूट' (discord, breach between people) specifically denotes interpersonal splitting; Arabic 'انقِسام/اِنْقِسَامٌ' (division, splitting) from the root q-s-m (to divide/distribute); Korean '분열' (分裂, splitting apart) and '분쟁' (紛爭, dispute) show both the structural and contentious aspects; Swahili 'mgawanyiko' (division) and 'mfarakano' (separation, discord) distinguish between the state of being divided and active estrangement.

A physical rending or tearing of cloth or material; used in Jesus' parable about not sewing unshrunk cloth on an old garment, lest the patch tear away and the tear become worse (Matt 9:16; Mark 2:21). This is a concrete, literal usage distinct from the metaphorical social-division sense. Spanish 'rotura' (rupture, break) specifically denotes physical damage to material; Hindi 'फटना' (tearing, ripping) is the verb-noun for cloth being torn; Arabic 'شَقٌّ' (crack, split, tear) and 'خَرقٌ' (hole, tear in cloth) both denote physical fabric damage; Korean '찢어짐' (being torn, the state of being ripped) uses the native Korean root for physical tearing; Swahili 'mwanya' (crack, gap) and 'mraruko' (tear, rip) distinguish between the resulting gap and the act of rending.
